city_center.name: Downtown Phoenix / Heritage Square
city_center.landmark: Camelback Mountain + South Mountain on the skyline; Heritage Square is the last intact 1890s residential block of the original townsite

cultural_notes: the Hohokam engineered the original canal network across the Salt River valley; freestanding adobe-walled compounds appeared roughly A.D. 1150-1200, and modern Phoenix canals trace that ancient irrigation (source: Culture History of Southern Arizona: Hohokam, statemuseum.arizona.edu)

Pueblo Revival is a signature historic-district style in Phoenix: sun-dried adobe or stucco/concrete stand-ins with rounded corners, irregular parapets and thick battered walls (source: Pueblo Revival architecture in Phoenix, historicphoenix.com; historicphoenixdistricts.com)
Sonoran Transitional and territorial-era adobe are documented local styles (source: Wisdom House NRHP nomination, nps.gov; Preservation of adobe, phgmag.com)
large snowbird / seasonal-resident population reshapes the fall-winter grocery calendar (INFERRED demographic framing -- verify tone before production use)
